Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:11:1.hebrew: חד לדיין - דבדיין מודו רבנן דשונא לא ידון, דלא מצי חזי ליה זכותא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:11:1.english: One for a judge - For regarding a judge, the Rabbis agree that an enemy may not judge, as he cannot see merit for him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:12:1.english: And the other - To disqualify two judges who hate each other [from sitting] in one judgment.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:13:1.english: They intimidate them - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:14:1.english: He said to me - The borrower said to me:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:14:2.english: He has said nothing - For a person is prone to say, 'So-and-so is my creditor,' so that [people] will not consider him wealthy.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:14:3.hebrew: הודה לו - שהיו שניהם בפנינו, להודות נתכוון, להיות לו עדים בדבר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:14:3.english: He admitted to him - [Meaning] that both of them were before us; he intended to admit, so that there would be witnesses for him in the matter.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:16:1.english: [If] two say: Exempt, and one says: Liable, [he is] exempt - As it is written: “To incline after the majority” (Exodus 23:2).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:16:2.hebrew: אפילו שנים מחייבין או מזכין והשלישי אומר איני יודע יוסיפו הדיינין - ואע"ג דאי הוה פליג עלייהו הוי בטל במיעוטא, כי אמר איני יודע הוי כמי שלא ישב בדין, ונמצא הדין בשנים, ואנן תלתא בעינן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:16:2.english: Even if two deem liable or deem exempt, and the third says, "I do not know," they must add judges - And even though, had he disagreed with them, he would be nullified in the minority, when he says, "I do not know," he is as one who did not sit in judgment, and the judgment is found to be [conducted] by two, and we require three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:17:1.hebrew: מכניסין אותן - לבעלי דינין. ובגמרא פריך: הא לא אפקינהו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:17:1.english: They bring them in - [This refers to] the litigants. And in the Gemara it asks: But they did not take them out [in the first place]?!

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:19:1.hebrew: היכי א"ל - לעדים כשמאיימין עליהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:19:1.english: How do we say to them - To the witnesses, when intimidating them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:19:2.hebrew: נשיאים ורוח וגשם וגו' - בשביל מתהלל במתת שקר, דהיינו מעידי שקר, גשמים נעצרים. ואפילו כשהשמים מתקשרים בעבים ורוח להוריד גשמים, אין הגשם בא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:19:2.english: Clouds and wind without rain, etc. - On account of [one who] boasts of a false gift — that is, false witnesses — rains are withheld. And even when the skies become overcast with clouds and wind to bring down rain, the rain does not come.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:1:1.hebrew: קרובים ונתרחקו הוו - שמתה אחותם, אשת מר עוקבא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:1:1.english: They were relatives and became not related - For their sister, the wife of Mar Ukva, had died.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:21:1.hebrew: אמר רבא - מאי איכפת להו אם לא ירדו גשמים? אמרי בלבם משל הדיוט: שב שני הוה כפנא, ואבבא אומנא לא חליף — על פתח מי שיודע אומנות ובעל מלאכה לא עבר הרעב:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:21:1.english: Rava said - What do they care if rain does not fall? They say in their hearts a common proverb: "Seven years there was a famine, but past the door of the craftsman it did not pass" — past the doorway of one who knows a craft and is an artisan, the famine did not pass.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:21:2.hebrew: מפץ וחרב וגו' איש עונה וגו' - בעון עדות שקר דבר בא, ויתייראו שלא ימותו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:21:2.english: “A hammer, and a sword, etc., a man who bears, etc.” - Due to the sin of false testimony, pestilence comes, and they will be afraid that they might die.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:23:1.hebrew: אאוגרייהו זילי - השוכרים אותם מבזים אותם, וקלים הם בעיניו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:23:1.english: Belittled by those who hire them - Those who hire them despise them, and they are held in low esteem in his [the hirer's] eyes.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:23:2.hebrew: והושיבו שנים אנשים בני בליעל - גבי נבות היזרעאלי כתיב, שיועצי המלך היו יועצים לשוכרם, והיו קורין אותם בני בליעל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:23:2.english: And set two men, base fellows - It is written regarding Naboth the Jezreelite, that the king's counselors were advising to hire them, and [yet] they called them "base fellows."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:24:1.english: In our presence - This implies that they made us witnesses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:26:1.hebrew: פטור - ואע"פ ששמעו עדים אתמול שהודה לו, הואיל ולא אמר "אתם עדיי":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:26:1.english: Exempt - Even though witnesses heard yesterday that he admitted to him, since he did not say: 'You are my witnesses.'

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:26:2.hebrew: משטה אני בך - שוחק הייתי בך, בשביל שהיית שואלני מה שלא היה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:26:2.english: I was teasing you - I was jesting with you, because you were asking me for that which never was.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:28:1.hebrew: הכמין - החביא, כמו ״וארב לו״ (דברים יט) — ״ויכמון ליה״:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:28:1.english: Hid - Concealed [them], as in: "and lie in wait for him" (Deuteronomy 19:11) — [which the Targum renders:] "and he shall lie in wait for him."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:29:1.hebrew: ואין טוענין למסית - המסית חבירו לעבודת כוכבים, אין טוענין אותו ב"ד בשבילו טענת זכות, אלא אם כן טוענה הוא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:29:1.english: And they do not advance a claim on behalf of an inciter - [Regarding] one who incites his fellow to idol worship, the court does not advance a claim of acquittal on his behalf, unless he claims it himself.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:30:1.hebrew: ואם לא טען - משטה הייתי בך כשהודיתי, אלא אמר: לא אתן לך, הבא עדים שהלוית לי — אין טוענין בשבילו, אלא אומרין לו: אחרי שהודיתה, לך שלם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:30:1.english: And if he did not claim - "I was teasing you when I admitted," but rather said: "I will not give [it] to you; bring witnesses that you lent to me" — they do not advance a claim on his behalf, but rather say to him: "Since you admitted, go pay."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:30:2.hebrew: ובדיני נפשות - אם יש טענת זכות והוא אינו יודע לטעון, טוענין לו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:30:2.english: And in [cases of] capital law - If there is an argument for acquittal and he does not know how to argue [it], [the judges] argue on his behalf.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:32:1.hebrew: לפי שלא טען - הנחש, לא טען הקב"ה בשבילו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:32:1.english: Because it did not claim - [Since] the snake [did not claim], the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not claim on its behalf.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:34:1.hebrew: ולא תגעו בו - הקב"ה לא הזהירם על הנגיעה, ומתוך תוספת גירעו — שדחף הנחש את חוה על האילן עד שנגעה בו. אמר לה: ראי שאין מיתה על הנגיעה, אף על האכילה לא תמותי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:34:1.english: Neither shall you touch it - The Holy One, Blessed be He, did not warn them against touching [it]; and out of the addition [came] the subtraction — for the snake pushed Eve against the tree until she touched it. He said to her: “See that there is no death for touching [it]; so too regarding eating, you will not die.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:35:1.hebrew: אמתים - דל אל"ף מהכא, קרי ביה (מתים) — הוי שתי מאות אמה. כל אותיות שבתורה הברתם ככתיבתם? כמו ועשית ואמרת — כאלו כתובה בה"א, וכן אתה חסר — כמו אותה מלא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:35:1.english: Two cubits - Remove the [letter] alef from here [and] read it as (matayim) — it is two hundred cubits. Is the pronunciation of all letters in the Torah according to their spelling? Just as [with] “ve’asita” and “ve’amarta,” [they are pronounced] as if written with a hei, and likewise [the word] ata [written] defectively is like it [written] fully.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:36:1.hebrew: עשתי עשרה - דל עיי"ן מהכא, הוו להו שתים עשרה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:36:1.english: Eleven - Remove [the letter] ayin from here, [and] it would be twelve.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:3:1.hebrew: בקבא דקירא אידבקי בכו - בקב של שעוה נדבקתי בכם? — בתמיה. כלומר: איני דבוק בכם כלל, אלא אתון לא צייתיתון דינא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:3:1.english: Am I stuck to you with a kav of wax - [Was I] stuck to you with a kav of wax? — [said] in astonishment. That is to say: I am not stuck to you at all; rather, you do not obey the law.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:5:1.hebrew: מיום ראשון ואילך - בטלה שושבינות, וכשר להעיד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:5:1.english: From the first day and onward - [His] groomsman status ceases, and he is valid to testify.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:6:1.hebrew: והוא לא אויב לו יעידנו - דהאי והוא אעד קאי, דמעיד שהוא חייב גלות, והעד לא אויב לו לרוצח. דאי ברוצח — הא כתיב (דברים ד) והוא לא שונא לו, וקראי אחריני טובא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:6:1.english: “And he was not his enemy” — he may testify about him - For this [word], “and he,” refers to the witness, who testifies that he [the killer] is liable to exile, and the witness is not an enemy to him, to the killer. For if [it referred] to the killer, behold, it is written: “and he did not hate him” (Deuteronomy 4), and many other verses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:6:2.hebrew: ולא מבקש רעתו ידיננו - דסמיך ליה "ושפטו העדה", וקאמר ר' יהודה דהאי "לא מבקש רעתו" אשופטים קאי. ולשון זה מצאתי בברייתא דסיפרי, ולא בסיפרי שלנו: "והוא לא אויב לו" — העד, "ולא מבקש רעתו" — השופט:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 29a:6:2.english: “Neither sought his harm” can judge him - Because “and the congregation shall judge” (Numbers 35:24) is juxtaposed to it, and Rabbi Yehuda says that this [phrase], “neither sought his harm,” refers to the judges. And this wording I found in a baraita of the Sifrei, and not in our Sifrei: “And he was not his enemy” — the witness; “neither sought his harm” — the judge.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 29a:33:1.hebrew: דברי הרב ודברי התלמיד - וא"ת: אם כן, כל מסית יפטר עצמו באותה טענה! ויש לומר: דדוקא נחש, שלא נצטוה שלא להסית, ולא נענש אלא לפי שבאת תקלה על ידו; אבל מסית, שנצטוה שלא להסית — נמצא כשמסית עובר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 29a:33:1.english: "The statement of the teacher and the statement of the student" - And if you say: If so, every inciter could exempt himself with that same claim! And one can say: [This applies] specifically to the snake, who was not commanded not to incite, and was punished only because a mishap came about through it; but an inciter, who was commanded not to incite — it turns out that when he incites, he transgresses.
